ai_show_review.summary: Incendiary Viola Lee Blues & soaring New Potato jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The two‑song set delivers a blistering Viola Lee Blues that showcases Garcia’s smoking guitar and Phil’s deep bass counterpoint. New Potato Caboose follows with an early‑era soaring jam, highlighted by strong vocals and Pigpen‑style organ textures. Recording quality is solid across the soundboard sources, though one tape runs slightly fast.
ai_show_review.review:
On August 4, 1967 at Toronto’s O’Keefe Center the Dead offered a brief but electrifying glimpse of their emerging jam instincts. Set 1 consists solely of “New Potato Caboose” and “Viola Lee Blues,” each stretched into exploratory passages that hint at the band’s future improvisational depth. Garcia’s guitar on “Viola Lee” is repeatedly described as smoking and inventive, weaving feedback‑laden counterpoint with Phil Lesh’s resonant bass lines. The “New Potato” performance features a bright vocal from Bob Weir and a loose, soaring feel that captures the raw energy of the late‑’60s era. While the recordings are incomplete—one cuts off before the set’s end—and one runs slightly fast, the soundboard sources retain enough clarity to let listeners hear the band in an early, experimental mode.

Among the three available tapes, the Hanno capture (gd67-08-04.sbd.hanno.16752.sbeok.shnf) stands out for its crispness and focus on the “Viola Lee” showcase, making it the recommended listening choice despite the abrupt finish. Fans of the Dead’s formative period will find this show a valuable snapshot of Garcia’s early‑year fire and Lesh’s foundational bass work.

best_recording.reason: Good clarity and strong capture of the standout Viola Lee Blues, making it the most listenable despite the incomplete set.

key_highlights: Garcia’s smoking guitar solo on Viola Lee Blues
Phil Lesh’s deep bass counterpoint throughout both jams
Bob Weir’s stronger‑than‑usual vocals on New Potato Caboose
Early feedback experiment at the end of Viola Lee (cut off in some releases)

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a smoking, inventive guitar performance, especially on Viola Lee Blues, with moments of zone‑playing brilliance.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides deep, resonant bass counterpoint that anchors the jams and adds depth to the improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Weir offers solid vocals on New Potato Caboose, noted as better than usual for this period.
